overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving its July 19, 2022 minutes about fifteen months late; staffing changes were no excuse, and the violation was not found intentional. No further remedy beyond compliance was ordered because the Board had already corrected it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to create and approve minutes of its July 19, 2022 meeting in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the undisputed facts, we find that the minutes of the July 19, 2022 meeting were not timely approved, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: On review, complainant alleged the failure to approve minutes was intentional; the AG noted this was not in the original complaint and declined to find intent.
allegations.key_passage: In any event, we decline to find that the violation was intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further remedial action ordered because the Board approved the minutes before the complaint was filed).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
